structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, then nearly every oceanic island or archipelago has at least one native bat in its natural range, and many bat species are endemic to islands, while non-volant terrestrial mammals are nearly absent from the same islands.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Pre-specify a list of oceanic islands and archipelagos of at least 1,000 km² that have never been connected to a continent (for example Hawaii, Azores, Canaries, Madeira, Cape Verde, Galápagos, Mascarenes, Comoros, Seychelles, Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Solomons, Marianas, Carolines, New Caledonia, Society Islands, Juan Fernández, Tristan da Cunha, Ryukyu). Use PHYLACINE present-natural range maps (Chiroptera). Pass if both hold. (1) At least 85% of the listed islands or archipelagos overlap at least one bat species' present-natural range. (2) At least 100 Chiroptera species are flagged Island.Endemicity = island endemic in Trait_data, and bats make up at least 20% of all island-endemic mammal species with a present-natural range. Check that non-volant native mammals (excluding humans and human-introduced taxa) occur on fewer than 30% of the listed islands, to confirm Darwin's contrast.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Fail if fewer than 70% of the listed oceanic islands or archipelagos overlap any bat's present-natural range, or if fewer than 50 bat species are flagged island endemic, or if bats make up less than 10% of island-endemic mammals. Results between the pass and fail thresholds count as inconclusive and are reported as such.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'ærial mammals' are Chiroptera. 'Almost every island' is read as at least 85% of a pre-listed set of oceanic islands and archipelagos of at least 1,000 km². 'Oceanic' means never land-connected to a continent, so continental-shelf islands are excluded. 'Endemic' means the species is flagged as island endemic in PHYLACINE (Island.Endemicity). Modern reinterpretation: PHYLACINE's present-natural ranges are modelled ranges on a coarse grid (about 96.5 km cells), so very small islands cannot be resolved and are excluded by the size threshold. Island membership of cells is assigned from a coastline layer such as Natural Earth. Anthropogenic introductions are excluded because the present-natural scenario omits them. Recently extinct island bats remain in the data and are noted in the results.

dataset.name: Data from: PHYLACINE 1.2: The Phylogenetic Atlas of Mammal Macroecology
dataset.why_it_fits: It covers all mammals, including Chiroptera, and gives an order-level field (Order.1.2) and an island-endemicity flag (Island.Endemicity) in Trait_data.csv. It also provides present-natural range rasters, which show where bats occur without human introductions. Fields used: Binomial.1.2, Order.1.2, Island.Endemicity, IUCN.Status.1.2, and the present-natural range rasters, compared against a pre-specified island list. The same range maps let non-volant mammals be checked on the same islands.
